newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat rises on Chicago and despite local rain.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat rises on Chicago and despite local rain.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures rose on Monday on Chicago's stronger tone despite good rain in Australia's eastern wheatbelt.
January 1998 sold 12 lots to add A$1.00 to A$178.00 on the trade.
Settlement prices rose virtually across the board, mostly by 50 cents to A$1.00, but with September 1997 up by A$4.00.
Garry Hopper of ANZ Futures Ltd said the Australian market was a little stronger in line with Chicago, which is up on dry weather and last week's USDA export sales report.
The easing Australian dollar would also be helping SFE wheat, he said.
Rainfall in Australia's eastern wheatgrowing regions could be expected to dampen local prices which might ease in coming days, he said.
